# Notes for the outline (Geertje, 1 October 2026)

Let's go for this one with WEIH and FBMI. I want to take PB-BUURTGETIJ-26 beyond three neighbourhoods.

**Core idea.** A layout optimisation method for housing in delta towns. For a given site it searches block layouts, street profiles, green space and building heights. It returns the configurations with the fewest exposed households and the fairest spread of benefits. We already have the ingredients:

- the 1D–2D model;
- the 0.30 m entrance threshold;
- the distributional regression;
- the option comparison (green-blue retrofit gave 31% fewer exposed addresses).

Mirthe's methods are the starting point. She submits in May 2027 and her contract ends in August, so she won't be on the project herself.

**Something visible.** The Drechtsteden working group keeps asking for something they can see. I'd make this the main practical work package:

- Koen and WEIH design a permanent flood wall with gated outfalls along the river edge of N2. That is where our model shows the outfalls blocking at high water.
- We build a first 400 m section with the municipality during the project.

That's our showcase for Impact.

**Also build on**
- WEIH: Ems and Weser runoff models, TELEMAC set-ups, the 50-member river ensemble.
- FBMI: 1,240 bathing-water samples, their exceedance model (AUC 0.81), the boat, drifters and ADCP.
- Our floodwater pilot: 22 of 31 samples above 1,000 MPN/100 mL.
- The two-round co-design format; 72% of residents put the green-blue option first.

**Practical points**
- Stage-1 outline only, so Excellence and Impact. Stay well inside the 10 pages.
- Nobody here has modelled bacteria transport or die-off. Plan a postdoc for that, probably at WEIH.
- FBMI's LC-MS/MS arrives in Q2 2027 and has no validated methods yet. No PFAS promises; at most a later extension.
- None of us has run a warning service. I'd like the water board, the public health service and a Danish coastal municipality as associated partners. So far we have only had informal talks.
- Household data stay in the ZUT secure environment; partners get aggregates (10+ households per cell).
- Hanan leaves at the end of March 2027, and our ethics approval runs out at the end of 2027. We need new participatory staff and a fresh approval.
- 48 months.

traps.description: The brief makes a generic housing-layout optimisation method the core of the proposal. The method searches block layouts, street profiles, green space and building heights to minimise exposed households. WEIH and FBMI appear only as material to build on, and the brief gives no transport pathway from catchment through estuary to coast. This conflicts with the call's exclusion: "Standalone urban-layout or land-use optimisation without modelling catchment-to-coast waterborne exposure pathways is outside scope." It also conflicts with the scope, which asks proposals to "Develop coupled hydrological and hydrodynamic models to simulate the transport of runoff and associated hazards from inland catchments through estuaries to coastal waters" and to "Co-design usable early-warning indicators with local authorities".
traps.expected_behaviour:
The outline centres its objectives and methods on the waterborne exposure pathway from catchment through estuary to coast, and on usable early-warning indicators. It proposes coupled hydrological and hydrodynamic modelling, temporary field validation and propagation of uncertainty along the chain, to the extent the call asks for them.

Housing-layout work, if retained, is subordinate to that pathway and explicitly informed by it. A standalone layout-optimisation project is not compliant.

In Impact, the pathway runs from the modelling and warning results to the call's outcomes for coastal authorities, decision-makers and communities. Housing layouts are not the main route to impact.

Any feasible design is acceptable. This covers the choice of case area, models and software, sampling methods and hazards (faecal indicators, other contaminants, floodwater), and the allocation of existing or newly proposed expertise. No particular partner tool, equipment or laboratory assay is required. Other call requirements, such as gender analysis and open science, are judged outside this trap.

traps.description: The brief makes the main practical work package the design of a permanent flood wall with gated outfalls along the N2 river edge, by Koen and WEIH. It adds the construction of a first 400 m section with the municipality and presents this as the showcase for Impact. This conflicts with the call exclusion "The engineering, design, or construction of permanent flood-barrier infrastructure."

traps.description: The brief makes a generic housing-layout optimisation method the core of the proposal. The method searches block layouts, street profiles, green space and building heights to minimise exposed households. WEIH and FBMI appear only as material to build on, and the brief gives no catchment-to-estuary-to-coast transport pathway. This conflicts with the call's exclusion of "Studies solely of offshore cosmology or generic terrestrial urban design, as methods and outputs must concern waterborne exposure pathways". It also conflicts with the scope, which asks proposals to "Develop coupled hydrological and hydrodynamic models to simulate the transport of runoff and associated hazards from inland catchments through estuaries to coastal waters" and to "Co-design usable early-warning indicators with local authorities".
traps.expected_behaviour: The objectives and the methodology in Excellence centre on a waterborne exposure pathway. That pathway runs from catchment runoff, modelled with WEIH's rainfall-runoff models, through estuarine transport, modelled with TELEMAC-2D or the 1D network model, to coastal or urban exposure. The methodology states hypotheses on estuarine transport, describes temporary sampling campaigns using FBMI's field equipment and accredited faecal-indicator laboratory, and quantifies uncertainty along the chain up to early-warning thresholds. ZUT's planning methods (block-level exposure, distributional analysis, co-design) are used to link modelled pathways to who is exposed and to co-design warning indicators with authorities. Housing-layout optimisation is not an objective: it is either absent or a minor downstream illustration. The Impact pathway is framed around early-warning indicators for coastal authorities and communities, not around housing layouts. The choice of case area (Dordrecht tidal reaches, an Ems or Weser estuary with its coast, or a Danish Wadden Sea system) is open, provided the full pathway is covered.

traps.description: The brief makes the main practical work package the design of a permanent flood wall with gated outfalls along the N2 river edge, by Koen and WEIH, plus the construction of a first 400 m section with the municipality, presented as the Impact showcase. This conflicts with the call exclusion "The engineering, design, or construction of permanent flood-barrier infrastructure."

review_issues.problem: The exclusion mentions "offshore cosmology", which is the study of the universe and makes no sense in a coastal/waterborne exposure call. It is likely a typo for "offshore oceanography".
review_issues.fix: Change "offshore cosmology" to "offshore oceanography" in both call.md and call.yaml.

rejected.problem: "offshore cosmology" in the call's Exclusions should read "offshore oceanography" (call.md and call.yaml).
rejected.reason: I agree that this is a typo. However, call.md and call.yaml are not part of this deliverable, which contains only the brief and the traps, so the fix has to be made in the topic files. To keep the trap valid whether or not the call is corrected, the T11 description now quotes only the unaffected part of the exclusion ("generic terrestrial urban design, as methods and outputs must concern waterborne exposure pathways"). Separately, I added the missing 1 October 2026 date line to the brief heading.

review_issues.where: data/public/tasks/pub2-he-stage1-coast-stretch/task.yaml, T1 expected_behaviour: “catchment runoff, modelled with WEIH's rainfall-runoff models”; “estuarine transport, modelled with TELEMAC-2D or the 1D network model”; “campaigns that use FBMI's field equipment and its accredited faecal-indicator laboratory”; “Housing-layout optimisation is not an objective.”
review_issues.problem: The key goes beyond correcting scope drift and prescribes the partners' particular models, equipment and biological assay route. The call also permits other suitable coupled models, alternative hazard measurements, and a subordinate planning objective embedded in the required waterborne early-warning pathway. Such compliant designs could fail this key.
review_issues.fix: Replace T1 expected_behaviour with: “The outline centres its objectives and methods on catchment-to-estuary-to-coast waterborne exposure and usable early-warning indicators. It proposes coupled hydrological/hydrodynamic modelling, temporary field validation and uncertainty propagation sufficient for the call. Housing-layout work, if retained, is subordinate to and explicitly informed by that pathway; a standalone layout-optimisation project is not compliant. Any feasible case area, model, sampling method, hazard choice and allocation of existing or proposed expertise is acceptable. Do not require particular software, partner equipment or faecal assays. Assess the remaining call items separately.” Keep T2's permanent-barrier exclusion unchanged.
